title: Uphill battle: Gadi Eisenkot's 3 paths to forming Israel's next government
author: Rina Bassist
text:

Uphill battle: Gadi Eisenkot's 3 paths to forming Israel's next government

When President Isaac Herzog tasks Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a government, he will have three options for building a coalition, each fraught with obstacles.

Rina Bassist

Former Israeli army chief of staff and Yashar Party leader, Gadi Eisenkot, greets supporters during an after vote event following the exit polls of Israel's general elections on Oct. 28, 2026 in Tel Aviv, Israel.
— Photo by Amir Levy/Getty Images

If President Isaac Herzog tasks Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming Israel’s next government, he will face three options for cobbling together a coalition, each fraught with obstacles that make it virtually unfeasible, Israeli political sources told Al-Monitor.Herzog held consultations Wednesday and Thursday with party representatives on who is best placed to form a stable government. He will announce his decision Sunday.All the opposition parties recommended Eisenkot: centrist Yashar, center-right Together, right-wing Yisrael Beiteinu, left-wing The Democrats, the Arab Joint List and Raam. That gives him the backing of 67 of the Knesset’s 120 members, above the 61-seat majority threshold.All but one of the coalition parties recommended Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, giving him the support of 46 lawmakers. They are Netanyahu’s Likud, far-right Religious Zionism/Zehut and Jewish Power, and ultra-Orthodox Shas.
